te.title: Fine crystals and a hungry let-down valve
te.sit: The centrifuge house complains that the cake has turned fine and wet over the last half hour. On the DCS PIC-102 has been opening more and more for the same charge, and the reactor pressure is creeping up.

te.title: V-202 level rock-steady
te.sit: For the last twenty minutes LI-221 has been drifting slowly downward and LIC-221 keeps closing its valve, yet the downstream vessels are losing level and the product flow is falling.

te.title: Third stage running hot
te.sit: The lab says the mother liquor from V-203 carries more TA than usual and TI-232 has been reading about 5 °C above its normal 218 °C for the last half hour. PI-230 is on its set point.

te.title: Two thermometers, one vessel
te.sit: The night shift reported that V-202 'runs hot' and suggested lowering PIC-220. TI-222 shows 249.5 °C.

te.title: 4-CBA off specification
te.sit: AI-252 shows 4-CBA in the product at about 106 ppm and rising (specification 25 ppm). p-Toluic acid, crystal size and all the crystallizer conditions look normal.

te.title: Less vapour to the header from V-202
te.sit: FI-229 (V-202 vapour to its header) has dropped from about 28 to 18 t/h, although PI-220, TI-222 and the charge are unchanged. The heat-recovery operator is asking where his steam went.

te.title: V-204 level climbing, valve wide open
te.sit: LI-241 has been climbing steadily and LIC-241 is now near 100 % output, while FI-255 is lower than usual. The centrifuge house says their receiver is fine.

te.title: V-204 level climbing again
te.sit: LI-241 is climbing and LIC-241 is opening, exactly as in last month's outlet plugging. The shift wants to cut the charge and rod out the outlet.

te.title: V-201 creeping up
te.sit: PI-210 has been creeping up for twenty minutes and is now above its alarm limit at about 50 bar; PCV-210 is fully open. The instrument technician has already checked PT-210 against a test gauge: it reads right.

te.title: Losing TA in the mother liquor
te.sit: The Balance and energy display shows TA lost in the mother liquor rising from 0.75 to about 0.95 t/h over the last half hour. The charge and the feed are normal.

te.title: V-201 hot with the pressure on set point
te.sit: TI-212 has been rising for twenty minutes and now reads about 5 °C above normal. PI-210 sits exactly on its set point. The product looks fine so far.

te.title: p-Toluic acid creeping up
te.sit: AI-251 (p-toluic acid in the product) has risen from about 70 to 100 ppm over the last hour and keeps climbing. The shift wants to raise the last-stage pressure to reject more p-TA.

meta.title: Troubleshooting report — TE-1 Fine crystals and a hungry let-down valve (PTA Multistage Flash Crystallizer)
meta.caseTitle: Fine crystals and a hungry let-down valve
meta.sit: The centrifuge house complains that the cake has turned fine and wet over the last half hour. On the DCS PIC-102 has been opening more and more for the same charge, and the reactor pressure is creeping up.

0.1.unit: Four agitated flash crystallizers V-201…V-204 in series take 250 t/h of 30 wt% terephthalic acid (TA) solution at 285 °C and 72 bar from the hydrogenation reactor R-101, through the let-down valve PCV-102 (PIC-102 holds the reactor pressure) and the SIS valve XV-105. Each vessel boils at its own pressure (48.66 / 34.47 / 23.09 / 10.85 bar a → 269.5 / 243.5 / 218.1 / 180.0 °C), the vapour goes to the heat-recovery headers (38 / 25 / 15 / 5 bar a) and the cooling crystallizes TA (50 / 85 / 95 / 99 % cumulative). Product: 169 t/h of slurry at 43.9 wt% solids, 120 µm mean size, p-TA 75 ppm, 4-CBA 16.5 ppm, to the centrifuges. Purge water 2.5 / 2.2 / 2.1 / 1.8 t/h flushes the level nozzles.

rows.what: Centrifuge cake “fine and wet over the last half hour”; the lab later: mean size 69 µm, many fines (00:32)
PIC-102 output rose from 50 % to 100 % (100 % at 00:27:00) at the same charge; PI-102 72.0 → 79.1 bar at 00:30 (HI 00:28:53)
TI-103 (feed temperature) 285.0 → 279.4 °C, flat from 00:15; first alarm TI-103 LO at 00:04:46

0.4.ctx: Day shift, unit lined out at design since the start of the record; no set point, mode or output changed by the board operator (event log); the reactor section was known to be working on its feed preheater; weather and utilities normal; the centrifuge house running normally until the cake changed.

R.1.p: Each crystallizer is a boiling vessel: its pressure (held by PIC-2x0 on the vapour valve) fixes its temperature through the water vapour pressure plus the boiling-point elevation, and the temperature fixes the solubility of TA (log10 S* = 0.016855 T − 3.1324). The feed enters above its saturation temperature, so all TA is dissolved until it flashes in V-201; the four stages cool it in steps so that the supersaturation per stage (S_flash 2.0 / 3.3 / 3.0 / 5.0) grows crystals rather than nucleating fines. Levels (LIC-2x1) give 16 min of residence time per stage; purge water keeps the level nozzles clear.

3.2.n: Solubility line: at 30 wt% TA (42.9 g/100 g water) the saturation temperature is 282.7 °C. TI-103 at 279.4 °C is 3.3 °C below it, so the feed is supersaturated in the let-down line itself — where there is no agitation, no crystal bed to grow on and the whole pressure drop across PCV-102. TA therefore crystallizes as fine nuclei in the line: part of it deposits on the trim (the valve passes less at the same output: 100 % and PI-102 rising), the rest enters V-201 as fines (V-201 soft-sensor size 26 µm). V-201 receives a colder feed that has already given up part of its crystallization heat upstream, so its flash falls (31.4 → 14.8 t/h) and the vapour that is not flashed in V-201 is flashed in V-202 (30.8 t/h against 28.2). The vessels themselves stay on their pressure–temperature pairs: the cause is upstream.

3.5.tree:
TOP: fine product with PCV-102 at 100 % and PI-102 rising
 OR — TA crystallizes in the let-down line (fines made upstream of V-201 AND the trim restricted)
      AND — feed colder than its saturation temperature (TI-103 < T_sat)  OR  feed stronger than its temperature allows (DI-104 ↑, killed)
 OR — PCV-102 mechanical fault (no fines expected, killed)
 OR — V-201 nucleating on its own (V-201 P and T off design, killed)
 OR — fines slug from upstream (PCV-102 untouched, killed)
 OR — TI-103 reading wrong (nothing else moves, killed)
3.5.cut: {feed below saturation temperature} — a single-element cut set; the valve restriction and the fines are two consequences of the same event, not two causes

5.1.proof: Ev-1, Ev-2, Ev-4, Ev-5, Ev-10, Ev-11; T-1 (reactor section: 279.4 °C, preheater), T-2 (fines, impurities normal), T-4 (FI-219 13.1 → 31.4 t/h and PIC-102 100 → 50 % after the preheat was restored)
5.1.mech: The reactor section's feed preheater lost duty → the feed arrived at 279.4 °C, 3.3 °C below the 282.7 °C saturation temperature of a 30 wt% TA solution → TA crystallized in the let-down line, where there is no agitation and no crystal bed: fine nuclei formed and part of the solid deposited on the PCV-102 trim → the valve passed less at the same output, PIC-102 opened to 100 % and the reactor pressure rose (79.1 bar a at 00:30, 90.3 bar a at the peak) while the charge fell → the fines went straight into V-201 (26 µm) and on through the train to the product (AI-253 88 µm at 00:30, lab 69 µm) → the centrifuge cake turned fine and wet. V-201 flashed less (14.8 t/h) because its feed was colder and had already given up part of its crystallization upstream.

rows.opt: Reactor section restores the feed preheat (TI-103 back above 283 °C)
Reactor section lowers the feed TA to 15 wt% (saturates at about 260 °C) until the preheater is back
Cut the charge to 200 t/h to protect the reactor pressure while the line clears
Alarm TI-103 against the saturation temperature computed from DI-104, with a margin of 2 °C

rows.step: Tell the shift supervisor the cause and the plan; stop line stays armed
Ask the reactor section to restore the preheat; agree a call-back when TI-103 > 283 °C
Tell the centrifuge house to expect fines for several hours and to segregate the product
Watch PI-102 against 91 bar a and FI-101; cut the charge if the line does not clear
Raise the alarm change (TI-103 against T_sat(DI-104)) through management of change

rows.act: Alarms acknowledged; reactor section telephoned; lab sample sent
Reactor section and lab replies logged; centrifuge house telephoned
Asked the reactor section to restore the feed preheat (TI-103 above 282.7 °C) — in the simulator the trainer clears the feed-temperature malfunction as the plant's answer; nothing moved on our DCS
Reactor section telephoned to confirm: Reactor section: "Charge 188 t/h at 284.7 °C, 30.0 wt% TA. Reactor at 89.2 bar."
End of record: TI-103 285.0 °C, PIC-102 50 %, PI-102 72 bar a, FI-219 31.4 t/h; AI-253 44 µm still under specification (fines in transit)

rows.pval: back toward 50 % as the line clears (slower — the deposit must redissolve)
back to 72 bar a once PCV-102 passes 250 t/h again
rising once no more fines come in (one residence time 16 min to show)
rising within the hour — WRONG: see 5.7

5.7.n: Three divergences. (1) The let-down line cleared slowly: PIC-102 stayed at 100 % for 20 min after the fix, FI-101 dipped to 147 t/h at 00:40:00 and PI-102 peaked at 90.3 bar a at 00:40:00 — 1.7 bar a below the charge pump dead-head and closer than planned; next time cut the charge to 200 t/h at the same time as the fix so the deposit redissolves at a lower pressure. (2) The product size kept falling after the fix (77 → 44 µm at +60 min): the fines already made are in transit through four vessels of 16 min each and the fine population dilutes out only over several residence times; V-201 is recovering first (26 → 80 µm). The AI-253 LO alarm was still standing at 01:34:00; the centrifuge house was told. (3) FI-255 swung (190 → 131 → 165 t/h) with the charge, as the levels were held — no action needed.

5.8.rule: If TI-103 falls below 283 °C (or DI-104 rises above 31 wt%), call the reactor section at once — before PIC-102 starts to open: whatever crystallizes in the let-down line ends up in the product.

6.0.n: Cause confirmed by the response to the fix (FI-219 back to 31.4 t/h, PCV-102 back to 50 %); the product size lagged by hours, which the prediction had missed.

rows.m: DCS alarm on TI-103 against the saturation temperature computed from DI-104 (T_sat(x) + 2 °C margin), not a fixed 283 °C
Preheater outlet temperature low alarm and call-out in the reactor section, with the crystallizer board operator on the distribution
Shift check: TI-103 − T_sat(DI-104) margin read once per shift from the Overview
This case in the operator training file (TE-1 worked example)

rows.i: PCV-102 protected from solids: no more trim erosion from crystallizing feed
The alarm on the margin also catches a feed that is too strong (DI-104)
Product under 90 µm for several hours after the fix: segregate and rework
The reactor pressure came within 2 bar of the pump dead-head during the recovery: a charge cut must be part of the fix procedure

hz.dev: LESS TEMPERATURE — feed to V-201 (below T_sat)
hz.cons: TA crystallizes in the let-down line: PCV-102 restricts, PI-102 rises toward the charge pump dead-head 92 bar a, fines to the product
hz.sg: TI-103 LO 283 °C (to become T_sat(DI-104) + 2 °C); PI-102 HI 76 bar a; the stop line (charge cut); R-101 relief (reactor section)

hz.cons: Same as above with TI-103 normal
hz.sg: DI-104 HI 31 wt%; the margin alarm

hz.cause: Solids on the trim; valve fault
hz.sg: PI-102 HI; charge cut; PSV on R-101 (reactor section)

hz.dev: LESS FLOW — charge after the fix
hz.cons: Levels fall; residence time rises; vapour to the headers swings
hz.sg: LI LO alarms 30 %; FI-101 LO 190 t/h

6.3.fut: An alarm limit must be a function of the operating condition when the physics says so (T_sat depends on the concentration). A fix that depends on another section needs a call-back time and a stop line of our own. Predict the recovery time as well as the direction.

6.4.how: One hour of design margin (60,900 USD/h, the simulator's price set): the feed trip on PI-102 / charge pump that a late fix would have caused, with the restart that follows.

6.5.again:
Check the feed against its saturation temperature first whenever fines appear with the let-down valve opening.
Ask the people who own the change (reactor section) before touching our set points.
Write the stop line before the investigation; keep it armed through the fix.
Use the cheap tests first: three telephone calls and a lab sample killed six of seven hypotheses.
6.5.never:
Never raise a crystallizer pressure to “grow bigger crystals” when the fines are made upstream.
Never wait for the product analyzer (5 min lag plus one hour of transit) to confirm what the first vessel already shows.
Never assume the plant recovers at the speed of the fix.

hyp.cause: Feed below its saturation temperature (reactor preheat lost)
hyp.ifthen: If TI-103 is below 282.7 °C the solution is supersaturated in the let-down line: TA crystallizes before V-201 — the deposit restricts PCV-102 (output ↑ at the same charge, PI-102 ↑) and the fines formed there go straight into V-201 and the product (AI-253 ↓); V-201 flashes less (FI-219 ↓).
hyp.key: TI-103 < 282.7 °C before PIC-102 output and AI-253 move; FI-219 ↓
hyp.fals: TI-103 ≥ 283 °C throughout, or the reactor section reports a normal preheat

hyp.cause: Feed TA concentration up (31 wt% or more saturates above 285 °C)
hyp.ifthen: If DI-104 rose above about 32 wt% the feed would be saturated at its own 285 °C: the same crystallization in the line, but with TI-103 unchanged and DI-104 HI.

hyp.cause: TI-103 reads low (transmitter bias) — the feed is really at 285 °C
hyp.ifthen: If only the thermometer is wrong, nothing else moves: PIC-102 output, PI-102, FI-219 and the product size stay on design.
hyp.fals: Any process variable moving with it; the reactor section reporting the same temperature

hyp.cause: Fines surge from upstream (start-up crystals flushed into the feed)
hyp.ifthen: If a slug of fines came in, the V-201 size would step down at once and recover; TI-103, PIC-102 output and PI-102 would not move.
hyp.key: V-201 size step ↓ then ↑; PIC-102 output steady
hyp.fals: PIC-102 output rising with the fines; TI-103 below saturation

hyp.cause: PCV-102 mechanical fault (trim / actuator) — the valve passes less at the same output
hyp.ifthen: If the valve itself were failing, PIC-102 output and PI-102 would rise but there would be no fines, TI-103 would be normal and FI-219 would hold until the charge fell.
hyp.key: PIC-102 output ↑ with AI-253 and TI-103 normal

hyp.cause: Agitator M-201 slowing or stopped — settling bed, attrition fines
hyp.ifthen: If M-201 were in trouble, JI-214 would fall or read 0 (JI LO), DI-254 would change and LIC-211 output would move; TI-103 and PIC-102 would not.

hyp.cause: V-201 pressure or temperature upset (PIC-210 off set point → supersaturation burst → nucleation)
hyp.ifthen: If V-201 nucleated on its own, PI-210 or TI-212 would have left design (T − T_sat − BPE ≠ 0) and FI-219 would have jumped, not fallen; PIC-102 would be untouched.
hyp.fals: PI-210 and TI-212 on design throughout

tests.title: Telephone the reactor section — feed temperature and the preheater
tests.move: Field ▸ Telephone: reactor section ▸ Ask about the feed (reply in 2 min). Nothing is changed on the plant.

WH-1.note: they report ≈ 279.4 °C and a preheater problem

WH-3.note: they report ≈ 285 °C — only our transmitter is wrong

WH-4.note: they report a normal temperature and mention flushing start-up crystals

tests.kill: If the reactor section reports the feed at 285 °C → WH-1 killed and WH-3 survives; if they report < 283 °C and a preheater problem → WH-3 and WH-4 killed.

res.obs: Reactor section: "Charge 230 t/h at 279.4 °C, 30.0 wt% TA. Reactor at 85.1 bar. Our preheater is struggling, outlet temperature is dropping." TI-103 on the DCS read 279.4 °C at the same time: the two readings agree; the preheater is the reported change.

tests.title: Lab sample of the product slurry — size, fines, impurities
tests.move: Field ▸ Product sample (lab) ▸ Take sample (result in 2 min). Nothing is changed on the plant.

WH-1.note: many fines, still falling while the line keeps making them; p-TA and 4-CBA normal

WH-4.note: a one-off slug would be growing out by now — size recovering

WH-6.note: fines with a thicker slurry (DI-254 ↑) and JI-214 off design

tests.kill: If the lab finds a normal size (≥ 90 µm) → WH-1 killed; if AI-253 is already rising → WH-4 supported; DI-254 ↑ with JI-214 off design → WH-6 supported.

res.obs: Lab (product slurry): mean size 69 µm, many fines under the microscope; p-toluic acid 75 ppm; 4-CBA 16.5 ppm; solids 43.7 wt%; TA dissolved in the mother liquor 0.79 wt%. AI-253 kept falling (88.0 → 77.2 µm by 0:34); DI-254 43.7 wt% (slightly thinner, not thicker); JI-214 49 A on design.

tests.title: Telephone the centrifuge house — what they see and take
tests.move: Field ▸ Telephone: centrifuge house ▸ Call (reply in 2 min). Nothing is changed on the plant.

WH-1.note: cake fine and wet from fines, solids content about normal, they take the higher slurry flow

WH-5.note: cake normal — a valve fault alone makes no fines

tests.kill: If the cake is normal → WH-1 weakened, WH-5 survives; if the cake is fine and wet → WH-5 killed (a valve fault alone makes no fines).

res.obs: Centrifuge house: "We are taking 190 t/h of slurry; cake looks fine and wet, it does not drain well." DI-254 43.7 wt% unchanged over the window.

tests.title: Restore the feed preheat (the reactor section) and watch V-201
tests.move: Field ▸ Telephone: reactor section — ask them to bring TI-103 back above 283 °C (they restore the preheater; in the simulator the trainer clears the feed-temperature malfunction as the plant's answer). Nothing on our DCS is moved; FIC-101 stays at 250 t/h with the stop rule armed.

WH-1.note: back toward 31.4 t/h within about 20 min of TI-103 regaining 283 °C; PIC-102 output comes back down as the line clears

WH-5.note: a mechanically failing valve does not care about the feed temperature

tests.kill: If FI-219 has not risen by 5 t/h within 30 min of TI-103 ≥ 283 °C → WH-1 killed, WH-5 back on the table.
tests.stop: Cut FIC-101 to 200 t/h if PI-102 reaches 91 bar a (charge pump dead-head 92 bar a) or LI-211 > 85 %; ESD if PI-210 approaches PSHH-218 (53 bar a).
tests.back: None needed — the move restores design conditions; the charge cut, if used, is returned to 250 t/h once PI-102 < 76 bar.

res.obs: TI-103 back to 284.7 °C at 00:44:00 and 285.0 °C by 0:45. FI-219 13.1 t/h at the move → 18.7 at +10 min → 31.1 at +30 min → 31.4 t/h at +60 min (design 31.4). The let-down line cleared slowly: PIC-102 stayed at 100 % until about 00:58:00, FI-101 dipped to 147 t/h at 00:40:00 and PI-102 peaked at 90.3 bar a at 00:40:00 (stop line 91 bar not reached), then PI-102 HI cleared at 00:56:13 and PIC-102 was back at 50 % at 01:27:00.
